reasons:
VERDICTS
undertow: KILL collision — its whole hook ('the machine that just proved you right is no longer the machine you learned') is g0002 Re-Pin's already-shipped core loop restated: deduce a hidden deterministic state, then your own correct play mutates it and rots your knowledge (Re-Pin: 'old knowledge rots and the crackers must decide whether to spend a turn re-testing a chamber they already know'). Same fun-correct-bet, different shell.
kick: KEEP — the bluff is resolved by real magnet physics with zero referee and a visible cascade (clamp/eject down the rail) that passes the moving-picture test outright; sharpest single mechanism of the five and the least like anything else in the batch or the archive.
warren: KILL taste — the spark's own fun_correct_bet admits the failure mode ('a player who ignores the sealed board and just yanks the mole toward home hands everyone else a free survey'), which means the rational move is to let opponents pay the turn-ending cost of discovery and win off their map for free — a no-cost-information design smell in the same family TASTE flags against tensionless mechanisms.
rattle: KILL taste — the signature motion (ball advancing chambers) happens sealed inside an opaque tile and is only ever visible through a private one-seat reader window; the public-facing action is just a hand tilting a small cube, so the fifteen-second moving-picture test TASTE.md demands has no shot to point a camera at.
slow-draw: KILL feasibility — the whole game stands on 24 bare-FDM print-in-place dashpots holding 0.15mm piston clearance and a 0.4-0.9mm drilled orifice, expected to give the same repeatable 1-9s air-damped fall every time with no gasket, lubricant, or post-process allowed under the magnets/rubber-bands-only exception list; FDM layer lines don't hold an airtight seal at that tolerance, so the one load-bearing mechanism is not printable as specified.
